question: Which Indian festival is a festival of lights?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Diwali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Known as the **Festival of Lights, Diwali** is one of the most popular and widely celebrated festivals in India.
 
• People celebrate by lighting **oil lamps (diyas)**, bursting firecrackers and worshiping deities like **Lakshmi** (goddess of wealth) and Lord **Ganesha**.
 
• Diwali marks the return of **Lord Rama to Ayodhya** after a 14-year exile and his victory over Ravana, according to the Ramayana.
 
• It is typically a five-day festival, with the main celebration on the third day, known as **Lakshmi Puja.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Holi** is celebrated primarily in northern India to welcome the **arrival of spring.**
 
• Holi signifies the **victory of good over evil**, particularly the burning of the demoness **Holika**.
 
• Holi falls on the **Purnima (full moon) day of the Hindu calendar month of Phalguna**, which usually occurs in March.
 
• There are **three types of Bihu celebrated in Assam**:
 
 
• **Rongali Bihu (Bohag Bihu)**: Celebrates the Assamese New Year and is a spring festival.
 
• **Kongali Bihu (Kati Bihu)**: A quieter festival, focused on prayer and lighting of lamps during the month of Kati.
 
• **Bhogali Bihu (Magh Bihu):** Celebrated in January to mark the end of the harvesting season.
 
 
 
• **Onam** is the **biggest festival in Kerala** and celebrates the legendary return of **King Mahabali.**
 
• One of the major attractions during Onam is the famous **snake boat races**, particularly in the** Pampa River**.
 
• Onam falls in the **Malayalam month of Chingam**, which usually occurs in August-September.
